guidelines.detail: refines FID-01 (The description explicitly states completion work after several outcomes, while the records report no counterpart for that work on those paths. FID-01 already requires modeling every distinct activity; this guideline specifies how to apply it to stated completion work.)

same as LRN-015 (The description identifies the decision outcome and deadline trigger (S6, S8), while the paired labels show semantic differences in how those elements are named (P1, P2). This wording is already covered by learned guideline LRN-015.)

new guideline (The description mentions the insurer and collection agency as communication endpoints but gives no activities for them. The generated pools and message flows therefore add collaboration elements not supported by the described work. The closest documented guideline concerns ordinary internal roles, and the learned guidelines do not already state this rule. The wording was checked and is not tied to)

same as LRN-026 (The description specifies activity-to-activity, start-to-activity, and branch-to-outcome connections that are absent from the generated model. The proposed guidance is already captured by learned guideline LRN-026.)

same as LRN-015 (S8 states that reaching the disagreement deadline without receiving money triggers forwarding the case. P1 shows a label describing that stated condition paired with a reference label that instead describes an unstated reminder milestone. LRN-015 already gives the same core instruction to preserve stated semantics rather than substitute a related meaning.)

refines COL-01 (The description attributes work to the narrator and describes communications involving other parties; the reference includes a participant pool for that work, while the generated model has no counterpart (C1). This refines COL-01 by clarifying when the narrated actor should be represented as a participant. LRN-032 concerns whether to add pools for external parties mentioned only in communication; )

refines FID-01 (The description explicitly states the action, while the generated model represents it with an extra exclusive gateway instead of the reference activity. This makes the difference a choice of BPMN element, not a missing action. The guideline refines FID-01 by specifying how to represent stated work when it follows a decision or another activity.)

same as LRN-015 (The description provides the semantics for these elements, and the label pairs show why labels should preserve those semantics. This is already essentially stated by learned guideline LRN-015.)

same as LRN-033 (The description uses a first-person narrator and describes communication with external parties, while the reference has a pool with no generated counterpart (C1). The proposed guidance is already essentially stated by learned guideline LRN-033. No generated-elements-without-counterpart records were provided to establish whether the actor was instead represented under another participant or lane.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly states that a matter is brought to completion after a decision or another activity: Model the stated completion work as an activity on the applicable path before the process outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly states that a matter is brought to completion after a decision or another activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states the action, purpose, recipient, scope, or outcome of a process element: Label the corresponding BPMN element with a concise phrase that preserves those stated semantics; do not substitute a related but different meaning, omit distinguishing details, or add unsupported details.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states the action, decision, or event trigger of a process element

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description mentions an external person or organization only as the recipient or source of a communication, without describing that party performing process activities or a separate process: Model the stated communication and any resulting wait or receipt within the described process; do not add a separate participant pool or message flows for that party.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description mentions an external person or organization only as the recipient or source of a communication, without describing that party performing process activities or a separate process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly states that an activity follows the process start or another activity: connect the corresponding BPMN elements with sequence flows in the stated order, preserving any intervening gateways and branches
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an activity, start, or decision outcome is followed by another activity or a process outcome

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description narrates work performed by a first-person actor and states that the actor communicates with people or organizations outside that work: Model the narrated actor as a participant pool in the collaboration, with the actor’s described work in its process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description narrates work performed by a first-person actor and states that the actor communicates with people or organizations outside that work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an actor performs a concrete action on a decision outcome or after another activity: Model the stated work as an activity on the applicable path. Use gateways to route or synchronize flow, not as substitutes for the work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an actor performs a concrete action on a decision outcome or after another activity
